items.title: Mrs. Francis Oliver Interview, 1969-05-10
items.q: He always wanted to be like Uncle Jerry. ... Jerry wrote him a nice letter, and he showed it to everybody.

ctx.x: I don't believe. I've been broke too. There's no disgrace to be broke. No, indeed. But I don't believe he had the money. The station can be broke sometimes.

He didn't hear I have enough money to send me home. I wish I had my son's college picture here to show you with the band at school. Yeah. Because he always wanted to be like Uncle Jerry. Oh, really? He always, and my brother wrote him such a nice letter when he was in school. He was in school from, let's see, 35 until 39. He graduated in 39. And Jerry wrote him a nice letter, and he showed it to everybody. Yeah. He was so pleased to have him, Uncle. That was in the musical world.
Yeah. Well, anyway, we're just about out of tape, and the next time I come, then we'll look at the, some of the photographs.
